Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

election noun

also elections, elect, be elected, election day, general election, hold an election, hold elections, stand for election, electoral, the polls, go to the polls, polling station, polling booth

classical

Plin. Ep. 3.20.2: comitiōrum diē, on election day
Traupman 179: comitia habēre, hold elections
M-O s.v. vote: election

comitia, comitiōrum n. pl.

noun, second declension, plural

elections; the Roman assemblies that elected the magistrates

The Roman people elected its magistrates in the comitia, named after the office at stake (comitia cōnsulāria, praetōria, tribūnicia); to hold an election is comitia habēre (Lewis & Short). Traupman and Morgan–Owens use the word for modern elections. A day on which the assembly could meet was a diēs comitiālis, Morgan–Owens’s election day (M-O; Liv. 25.2.4: prīmō comitiālī diē).

Other words

  • creō, creāre, creāvī, creātum — elect (a magistrate)

    verb, first conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Cic. Sest. 137: magistrātūs annuōs creāvērunt; Caes. BC 3.1 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 179: elect

    The usual verb for choosing magistrates, of the voters and of the officer who presided (Lewis & Short): cōnsulēs creāre. Traupman gives coöptāre for the choice of Roman senators.

  • creātiō, creātiōnis f. — the election of a magistrate

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Leg. 3.10: creātiō magistrātuum

    Rare (Lewis & Short).

  • ēlēctiō, ēlēctiōnis f. — an election (of a pope or an emperor)

    noun, third declension · also used · Renaissance · M-O s.v. vote: election (Turselinus, 1652); Cic. Or. 68: a choice (Lewis & Short)

    Classically a choice or selection (Cicero, Quintilian); the sense “election” is the Church’s and the Empire’s, as in Morgan–Owens’s seventeenth-century source.

  • saepta, saeptōrum n. pl. — the voting enclosure: the polls

    noun, second declension, plural · also used · classical · Cic. Mil. 41 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 180: polls, polling booth

    The great enclosure on the Campus Martius where the Roman people voted (Lewis & Short); Traupman uses it for the polls, and saeptum for a polling booth.

Examples

  • Proximīs comitiīs in quibusdam tabellīs multa joculāria atque etiam foeda dictū, in ūnā vērō prō candidātōrum nōminibus suffrāgātōrum nōmina inventa sunt.

    At the last election some ballots were found to have plenty of jokes on them, and even obscenities, and one had the names of the voters instead of the candidates.Plin. Ep. 4.25.1

  • omnēs comitiōrum diē tabellās postulāvērunt

    on election day they all asked for ballotsPlin. Ep. 3.20.2

See also vote, office, political, party.
